title: Solid Yellow, Do Not Pass
hook: A dead van sits ahead. The yellow on your side is solid.
scene: Clear cold afternoon. A Kent school zone with a solid yellow on your side. You want around a parked delivery van that has been dead since the first week. The van sits legal enough. Passing would put you over the solid. The playground is empty. The line is not. Hollis is not in this one. Nobody is coming the other way that you can see. That is the trick of a solid yellow: the thing you cannot see yet still owns that paint.
decision: A dead van is blocking your speed and the yellow under you is solid. Do you go around?

options.text: Stay behind the van until you can pass where the yellow breaks, even if that is slow
options.result: You wait. A block later the yellow breaks. You check, pass, and recover before the next solid. A car you did not have comes the other way in the gap you would have occupied. The van stays dead. You stay in your lane.

options.text: Go around now — nothing is coming and the van is the real hazard
options.result: You cross the solid. The other car was in the school-zone dip. Two plows of width, one lane, a freeze. You dive back and scrape the van. Paint on primer. The yellow was not decorative.

options.text: Straddle the yellow to peek, then decide
options.result: You are already in their lane to peek. Peeking is occupying. The dip car has to take the curb. You learned the sightline by stealing it.

options.text: Use the parking lane on the right to sneak past without crossing yellow
options.result: The parking lane is a door zone of ghosts. A van door that was not quite latched opens into your mesh. You pass the delivery van and inherit a different one. Right was not free. It was unsearched.

debrief: A solid yellow on your side means do not pass. Wait for the broken yellow and a sightline. The parked van is a delay. Ali waits until the yellow breaks.

source.psdp_skill: Skill five: driving on a quiet street – part one
source.teaching_target: Do not pass on a solid yellow line on your side; wait for a broken line and adequate sight distance.

The Beetle is nearer the bottom of the frame (rear mesh toward camera, plow pointing up-frame). The van is ahead of it in the SAME lane, also rear toward camera — windshield, grille, and headlights of the van are NOT visible. An entire empty oncoming lane sits between the yellow centerline and the left curb. Neither vehicle is left of the yellow. They are not nose-to-nose.
